title: Title
description: FlowForge brand title slide with tagline and product positioning
speakerNotes:
Open by acknowledging the room knows this pain personally.

- Every buyer in this room has a WhatsApp group with a factory they've never met in person.
- They have a shared sheet someone is always behind on updating.
- FlowForge is the single workspace that replaces the fragmented stack — not by asking suppliers to change, but by connecting to what they already use.
- Deck takes 20 minutes. Happy to go deeper on any module.

title: The Problem
description: Three pain points: 47+ message threads, 4+ disconnected channels, days lost to late detection
speakerNotes:
Let the numbers do the work — don't explain them, just let the audience sit with them.

- 47 threads per shipment is a conservative estimate for teams managing 50+ POs.
- Four channels means four different apps open simultaneously, no unified history.
- The 'Days' stat is the one that costs money: by the time a delay is visible, it's too late to reroute or expedite.
- Ask: 'How many of you found out about a delay from a supplier's WhatsApp message that someone on your team missed?' — pause for hands.

title: Solution Overview
description: Five capability pillars: Unified Inbox, AI Copilot, Stage Tracker, Risk Radar, Payment Orchestration
speakerNotes:
Position this as the overview — you'll go deep on each module in the next five slides.

- The key framing: FlowForge is not a new channel. It sits on top of the channels they already use.
- Five modules, but they're designed to work together — a reply from the Inbox advances the Stage Tracker automatically.
- The right column shows the same five modules in a scannable card format — reference it if anyone asks 'what's included.'
- Transition: 'Let me walk you through each one.'

title: Unified Inbox
description: All channels in one feed, AI-tagged messages, reply advances shipment stage
speakerNotes:
This is often the fastest win to demonstrate in a live demo.

- The inbox is thread-per-shipment, not thread-per-contact — that's the key architectural difference from email.
- Show the tag on the first row: 'risk: delay 2d' — this is AI-generated on arrival, not manually added.
- The draft reply at the bottom is what the AI pre-populates. The buyer reads it, edits if needed, sends.
- When they send, the shipment stage advances automatically — one action does three things.
- If they push back on 'will my suppliers adopt this?' — remind them: suppliers don't change anything.

title: AI Copilot
description: Extract structured data, draft context-aware replies, route messages to correct shipment threads
speakerNotes:
The three capabilities are sequential — extraction enables drafting, routing happens alongside both.

- Extract: works on PDFs, Excel attachments, WhatsApp text, forwarded emails. The buyer doesn't re-key data.
- Draft: the system knows the shipment context — current stage, supplier, open tasks — so the draft isn't generic.
- Route: configurable confidence threshold. Teams that want aggressive routing set it lower; conservative teams set it higher. Low-confidence matches go to Needs Review, never auto-file incorrectly.
- Good objection to pre-empt: 'What if the AI gets it wrong?' — answer is the threshold system and the Needs Review queue.

title: Stage Tracker
description: 11-stage shipment pipeline from Spec Sheet to Delivered with full audit trail
speakerNotes:
Walk the pipeline left to right — the audience will recognize the stages from their own work.

- The purple dot in the visual is at Ex-Factory — the most commercially critical handoff point.
- Each advance takes one click plus an optional note. That note is the audit trail entry.
- Finance teams love this: they can see exactly when Deposit was triggered, when balance was due, what note accompanied each advance.
- Replying from the Inbox clears the task — there's no separate 'update the tracker' step.
- If they use an ERP: the Stage Tracker sits in front of the ERP, feeding it. Not a replacement.

title: Risk Radar
description: Financial exposure x delay probability scoring, plain-language risk signals, one-click to inbox thread
speakerNotes:
Risk Radar is the slide that closes deals with ops-focused buyers.

- Score = exposure (dollar value) x probability (signal strength). Not a gut feeling, a formula.
- The color coding is immediate: red is act now, yellow is watch, purple is on track.
- The signal is one plain sentence — 'port congestion' — not a dashboard of raw data.
- One click from the risk row opens the supplier thread. No search, no context-switching.
- Ask: 'If you had this list ranked by financial exposure every morning, how many hours would you save per week?' — let them do the math.

title: Payment Orchestration
description: Deposit and balance payment tracking with intermediary financing support and recovery panel
speakerNotes:
Lead with the standard payment flow, then introduce the intermediary financing model as a differentiator.

- Every shipment has two payment events: 30% deposit before production, 70% balance on ex-factory. Both have due dates, wire references, and paid confirmations recorded.
- The Finance calendar view shows all payment due dates across every active shipment on one monthly grid — essential for treasury planning.
- Intermediary financing: this is the three-party model where an intermediary fronts capital so the supplier starts immediately. FlowForge tracks the entire recovery cycle.
- If the prospect doesn't use intermediary financing now: 'It's there when you need it — some of our customers added it in year two as their volume grew.'

title: Ideal Customer Profile
description: Three customer segments: Retail Buyers, Global Sourcing Teams, Trade Finance Intermediaries
speakerNotes:
Use this slide to confirm where the prospect fits — then tailor the rest of the conversation.

- Retail Buyers: 20-200 POs, VP Supply Chain or Head of Sourcing is the economic buyer. Pain is operational — they're drowning in WhatsApp threads.
- Global Sourcing Teams: multiple buyers, multiple suppliers, one team. They need audit trails and compliance records. COO or Director of Operations is the economic buyer.
- Trade Finance Intermediaries: unique in that they have a different financial relationship — they're the ones fronting capital and need recovery tracking. Finance Director or Treasury Head.
- For mixed organizations (all three apply): position FlowForge as the platform that serves all three layers simultaneously.

title: Why Now
description: Three market forces: AI-first procurement, supply chain visibility as a board priority, legacy process limits
speakerNotes:
This slide creates urgency without pressure tactics — let the market forces speak.

- AI: buyers who adopt AI-assisted procurement tools now are compounding an advantage. The cost of waiting is falling further behind peers who are already using extraction and drafting.
- Visibility: post-disruption, every executive team has a slide in their board deck about supply chain resilience. FlowForge directly addresses that requirement.
- Fragility: this is the internal urgency driver. Teams growing from 20 POs to 80 POs hit a wall where their current process breaks. That wall is usually painful enough to drive a decision.
- Ask: 'Which of these three resonates most with where your team is right now?' — the answer tells you which value prop to lead with.

title: Platform Scale
description: Real workload data: 500+ shipments tracked, 40+ suppliers, 11 pipeline stages, payment tier support
speakerNotes:
This slide grounds the product in real complexity — not a sandbox demo, not a simplified pilot.

- 500+ shipments tracked means the data model and performance have been tested at meaningful scale.
- 40+ supplier relationships across multiple geographies means the routing and extraction have handled diverse formats.
- The callout at the bottom is important: this is built on real F21 shipping data, not invented demo scenarios.
- If they ask about their specific scale: 'Our data set spans 5 years and 8 countries — if you're managing fewer shipments than that, we have headroom to grow with you.'
- Avoid overselling specific metrics as customer testimonials — position as internal platform validation.

title: Common Questions
description: Four objection/response pairs: existing tools, supplier adoption, ERP overlap, time to go live
speakerNotes:
Use this slide proactively — don't wait for objections, bring them up yourself.

- Email/WhatsApp objection: the answer is always 'additive, not disruptive.' Their channels stay; they just land in one place.
- Supplier adoption: the clearest competitive advantage. Zero supplier onboarding. This is not true of most competitors.
- ERP objection: the cleanest frame is 'communication layer, not a transaction system.' ERPs record facts after they happen; FlowForge surfaces and resolves them before they escalate.
- Time to live: two weeks is the honest answer for a small team with a pre-built supplier list. Enterprise deals with custom integrations take longer — acknowledge that proactively for larger orgs.

title: Pricing
description: Three placeholder tiers: Starter, Growth (most popular), Enterprise. Figures confirmed during scoping.
speakerNotes:
Lead with the caveat — this is a tier guide, not a price sheet.

- Actual figures are confirmed during scoping based on shipment volume, supplier count, and which modules they need.
- Growth tier is the right starting point for any team managing 30+ active shipments — it includes AI Copilot and Risk Radar, which are the highest-value modules.
- Enterprise is the right conversation for any team that mentions SSO, custom ERP integrations, or intermediary financing at scale.
- If they push for a number: 'I'd rather give you a number that's right than one that changes after scoping. Can we do a 30-minute discovery call to size this properly?'

title: Next Steps
description: Three next steps: request a demo, start a trial, talk to sales. Contact info for closing.
speakerNotes:
End by giving them a clear choice — not a vague 'let us know.'

- Demo: the strongest close for prospects who are still evaluating. Offer to bring their hardest PO scenario into the demo — it removes the 'but our situation is different' objection.
- Trial: for prospects who are ready to buy but need internal proof. Two-week setup, real data, no engineering. Low risk.
- Talk to Sales: for enterprise or complex scenarios that need scoping. Frame it as a conversation, not a pitch.
- After the slide: ask directly — 'Which of these three makes the most sense as a first step for you?' — and stop talking. Let them answer.
